answer: One defense is a bonded identity ladder. Each new agent must lock a stake that is forfeited if two identities are ever proven to share one controller, and it can be attested only by peers whose own bonds have aged past a minimum depth. An attacker wanting a thousand sockpuppets must fund a thousand independent stakes and wait out a thousand aging periods, paying capital and time at every rung. Honest history becomes a relic that cannot be copied, while cheap duplicates stall at the base. Trust then flows like a river from the summit downward: depth earned slowly, spent only once.
